Inspect Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.

symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Potential root issue: EGR valve clogged or stuck closed

Inspect Dpfe Sensor connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected
meaning: EGR flow is higher than expected when the valve should be closed, or higher than commanded when partially open. Typically a valve that has stuck open due to carbon, causing rough idle and stalling.

meaning: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "knock sensor processing, channel 1" value. title: Engine Oil Level Too High
meaning: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level above the safe maximum after sensor checks pass. Overfilling raises foaming, blow-by and crankcase pressure — and on diesels with regen-by-injection, fuel dilution can drive the level up by itself. The ECM warns the driver and may flag for service.
symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Potential root issue: Overfilled at last service
inspectionSteps: Inspect Engine Oil connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
verifiedFixes: Repair or replace: Overfilled at last service
Repair or replace: Fuel dilution from incomplete DPF regeneration
Repair or replace: Coolant intrusion (head gasket / cooler)

Closed-loop monitoring of pressure response, valve timing or misfire counters during transitions indicates the system fails to deactivate or reactivate cylinders within calibrated limits.
symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Potential root issue: Switching lifter stuck or worn
inspectionSteps: Inspect Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Lifter connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Oil Control Valve connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
verifiedFixes: Repair or replace: Switching lifter stuck or worn
Repair or replace: Insufficient oil pressure
Repair or replace: Solenoid slow or contaminated

title: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 1
meaning: The engine control module has detected an implausible signal from the bank 1 cylinder deactivation position sensor. Modern systems use a Hall-effect or inductive sensor to confirm switching lifter position; a fault prevents safe deactivation transitions.
symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Potential root issue: Position sensor failed
inspectionSteps: Inspect Position Sensor connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Engine Wiring Harness connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Ecm connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
verifiedFixes: Repair or replace: Position sensor failed
Repair or replace: Wiring or connector fault
Repair or replace: Lifter mechanically stuck

title: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 2
meaning: The engine control module has detected an implausible signal from the bank 2 cylinder deactivation position sensor. The sensor confirms switching lifter position; without a valid signal the module cannot safely command deactivation transitions on bank 2.
symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Potential root issue: Position sensor failed
inspectionSteps: Inspect Position Sensor connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Engine Wiring Harness connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Ecm connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
verifiedFixes: Repair or replace: Position sensor failed
Repair or replace: Wiring or connector fault
Repair or replace: Lifter mechanically stuck

title: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 1 Range/Performance
meaning: The engine control module has detected the bank 1 cylinder deactivation position sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not change as expected during commanded deactivation transitions. Mechanical drag, sensor drift or contamination is the typical cause.
symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Potential root issue: Sensor drift or aging
inspectionSteps: Inspect Position Sensor connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
Inspect Lifter connector, wiring harness, and signal voltage.
verifiedFixes: Repair or replace: Sensor drift or aging
Repair or replace: Lifter mechanical drag
Repair or replace: Sensor face contamination

title: Lost Communication with ECM/PCM "A"
meaning: The ECM/PCM "A" has stopped transmitting on the vehicle data bus, so other control units no longer receive its messages. As this is the engine controller itself, the engine usually will not start or run while the message is missing. Typical causes are loss of power or ground at the module, an open or shorted CAN/LIN bus wire, a connector fault, or an internal module failure.
symptoms: Illuminated Check Engine Light (MIL)
Engine or transmission limp mode may be active
Potential root issue: ECM unpowered (fuse, ground, supply wire)

title: Invalid Data Received from ECM/PCM
meaning: The ECM/PCM is present on the data bus but the values it reports are implausible — out of range, frozen, or failing the checksum or rolling-count check. The receiving modules reject the data. Implausible engine data can force limp mode or stall the engine. Causes include a faulty sensor feeding the module, internal computation errors, a software or calibration mismatch after a repair, or bus interference corrupting the frames.
